title: Community transport
source_note: Original ForLanguage content. User-provided recent-review notes were used only as topic-frequency signals. British Council materials were used only to verify public task format and word limits.

tasks.prompt: You have joined a neighbourhood travel group. Reply briefly to five member messages.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.
questions: How do you usually travel around your city?
Which journey do you make most often?
What transport problem annoys you most?

tasks.prompt: The group is collecting ideas for better local transport. Write a short message describing one change that would improve your daily journey.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.

tasks.prompt: Members are discussing transport priorities in the neighbourhood.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.
questions: Should the city add more buses or improve walking and cycling routes?
What would make public transport more attractive?
How can transport changes help both residents and the environment?

tasks.prompt: The group receives news that a popular bus route will run less often next month. Write to a friend explaining how this could affect local people and what you think the group should do.
tasks.review_note: Original ForLanguage task authored from recurring practice/review themes and checked against the public Aptis ESOL General Writing format; no official or recalled prompt copied verbatim.

tasks.prompt: Write a formal email to the local transport office about the reduced bus service. Describe the likely impact and suggest changes that could maintain access without greatly increasing costs.
